messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SLO breach detected for tenant=graphleaf on /v2/stream (p99 streaming tail = 4.8s, SLO=2.0s). Sustained for ~6m. Auto-page to oncall. dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/d/streaming?s=graphleaf
oncall-elaine: Paging — I'm on it. Thanks bot. Starting triage. :mag_right:
miguel: I can take runtime side. Any sign it's multi-tenant?
jia: Pulling logs & KV cache metrics. Quick notes: KV cache evictions spiked at the same time as p99, concurrent sessions ~220 (typical is 20). Looks single-tenant burst.
sam-prod: Graphleaf confirmed spike from their internal job that fanouts many long prompts. They just pushed a batch job.
ryan-ops: Confirmed unusual prompt shape: lots of 6k+ token prefixes + embedded code blocks. Streaming chunk size drops to single-token flushes -> stall behaviour.
jia: paste of relevant snippet:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z stream_stall count=13 tenant=graphleaf session=abc123 kvcache_evictions=904 active_sessions=218
2026-03-15T14:03:02Z response_chunk_ms=1200 last_chunk_ms=1800 token_flush=1
```

miguel: hypothesis: KV-cache thrash for very long prefixes + high concurrency causing per-token path to block on cache misses and kernel context switches. Also notice exec queue depth saturated on host pool gw-rt-7.
oncall-elaine: Immediate mitigations we can attempt now (short-lived):
- route Graphleaf to fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint (model: rwd-small-v1)
- throttle/limit long requests > 3000 tokens for this tenant for 10m window
- scale up dedicated pool by +2 GPUs (if capacity available)
- if needed, enable temporary prefix-compact caching mode for Graphleaf

jia: I'm going to flip the route to fallback and add a quick rate-limit. Running command: 
```
# set canary route -> small model
redwood route set --tenant graphleaf --endpoint /v2/stream --model rwd-small-v1 --weight 100 --reason "emergency fallback for tail latency"
# add temp token cap
redwood quota set --tenant graphleaf --endpoint /v2/stream --max_tokens_per_request 3000 --ttl 10m
```

miguel: Scaling request issued to dedicated autoscaler: +2 GPUs to pool graphleaf-dedicated (policy: immediate-burst). If autoscaler fails, fallback will stay.
ryan-ops: I also cleared local KV caches on gw-rt-7 and gw-rt-9 to avoid cold eviction storm: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/hosts/gw-rt-7/kvcache/evict`
oncall-elaine: Done. Please verify metrics after 60s.

<moment passes>

miguel: Metric check: p95 went from 1.2s -> 1.1s (no issue), p99 dropped from 4.8s -> 1.7s after route flip + throttle + cache evict. Active sessions down to 65. Looks promising.

sam-prod: Customer impact? Graphleaf requests dropped but still serving; jitter reduced. Need to coordinate comms.
lucy-support: Drafting message to Graphleaf ops: "We observed a high-concurrency job causing KV-cache thrash and elevated tail latency. We applied a temporary fallback model and rate-limits to stabilize latency. Engineering will investigate root cause and recommend a durable fix." Will post to their support channel in 10m.
jia: Collecting traces to confirm root cause. Two suspicious patterns: repeated very long identical prefixes (could have been unbounded tokenization leading to repeated cache misses) and many parallel sessions from same API key.
miguel: Longer-term fixes on eng-run backlog:
- prefix compaction for very long prompts (avoid loading giant KV snapshots)
- adaptive per-tenant cache sizing + admission control
- smarter streaming flush heuristics to coalesce small chunks
- rate-limit policies for batch/async jobs hitting streaming endpoints

oncall-elaine: Handoff: I'll hand this to eng-runtime (miguel/jia) for RCA and postmortem. On-call will monitor for 2h. Handoff timestamp: 4465021800. If anything regresses, re-paging.

lucy-support: Note for incident report: impacted tenant: Graphleaf, duration ~6m of breach before mitigation, mitigations applied: fallback model route, temporary token cap, KV cache evict, +2 GPUs to dedicated pool. Severity: P2 (customer-visible latency).
sam-prod: Assign AE to coordinate follow-up with Graphleaf; also prepare billing/logs for potential excess capacity usage.

oncall-elaine: Thanks everyone. Marking thread as active handoff -> eng-runtime. Will attach graphs & traces to incident ticket. :white_check_mark:
